claims_to_verify: '10+ hard sets per muscle, per week': Schoenfeld, Ogborn & Krieger, J Sports Sci 2017;35(11):1073-1082 — dose-response up to ~10 weekly sets; the <5 / 5-9 / 10+ categorical comparison was only a trend (p=0.074). Phrasing '10+' with 'Based on' is the honest level.
'Most lifters grow well between 10 and 20': coaching consensus; research above ~10 sets is thinner. Not attributed to the study on purpose.
'You don't need to hit failure. You just need to get close.': consistent with Refalo et al., Sports Med 2023;53(3):649-665 (no clear advantage of training to failure for hypertrophy).
'1-3 reps before failure' and 'Add 2-3 sets, not 10': common coaching heuristics, not from a single study.
'Split them over 2 days': framed as practicality (quality of sets), not as 'frequency builds more muscle' — volume-equated research shows frequency matters little.
